title: Gold vs Nifty 50: Post-Tax Returns on ₹1 Lakh Over 20 Years
description: Over the last two decades, physical gold and Nifty 50 have shown different growth trajectories. Gold's returns are subject to Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG) t.

faq.q: What is indexation benefit for capital gains?
faq.a: Indexation benefit adjusts the purchase price of an asset for inflation, reducing the taxable capital gain. This is applicable for LTCG on assets like gold and real estate.

faq.q: Do I get indexation benefit for Nifty 50 investments?
faq.a: No, for long-term capital gains from equity shares or equity-oriented mutual funds (like Nifty 50 index funds), there is no indexation benefit.

faq.q: Is physical gold or Gold ETF better for investment?
faq.a: Gold ETFs offer better liquidity, no storage costs, and better purity assurance compared to physical gold. However, physical gold holds traditional and cultural value for many.

faq.q: How is Nifty 50 LTCG tax different from gold LTCG tax?
faq.a: Nifty 50 (equity) LTCG is taxed at 10% on gains above ₹1 lakh per financial year, without indexation. Gold LTCG is taxed at 20% with indexation benefit after three years.

faq.q: What is the ideal allocation to gold in a portfolio?
faq.a: There's no one-size-fits-all answer. Many financial experts suggest a 5-15% allocation to gold for diversification and as a hedge against inflation and market volatility, depending on individual risk appetite.

faq.q: Are dividends from Nifty 50 funds taxed?
faq.a: Yes, dividends received from equity mutual funds or ETFs are fully taxable in the hands of the investor as per their applicable income tax slab rates.
